arguments.summary: APT-29 conducted reconnaissance from external IP 203.0.113.88, which performed an Nmap scan against internal asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). The source IP was later observed initiating outbound connections from compromised engineering workstation WS-ENG-015. Although initial lateral movement and C2 activity were not fully detected by existing rules, firewall controls successfully blocked further communication after incident confirmation. No evidence of data exfiltration or ransomware deployment was found during analysis. Affected systems include WS-ENG-015, WS-ENG-022, and SRV-BUILD-01, all within the engineering subnet.

EDR query on WS-ENG-015 revealed chrome.exe with suspicious network connections. No malicious processes detected in process tree.
SIEM correlation identified anomalous PowerShell activity across engineering workstations. Retrospective search revealed missed alerts.
Firewall rule FW-RULE-0029 deployed to block outbound traffic to 203.0.113.88.

arguments.summary: An investigation into a suspected APT-29 intrusion revealed initial access via IP 203.0.113.88, which conducted a port scan against WS-IT-101. The threat actor likely pivoted using compromised credentials (CORP\helpdesk) to access internal engineering assets. While no malicious payloads were confirmed on WS-ENG-015, a keylogger (Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D) was detected on WS-ENG-022. No evidence of data exfiltration or C2 beaconing was found during analysis. Detection gaps were identified in credential misuse and encrypted C2 monitoring.

Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 to internal network using CORP\helpdesk credentials.
EDR query on WS-ENG-015 showed normal user activity; no suspicious processes or network connections.
Full EPP scan on WS-ENG-022 identified and quarantined Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D in /usr/sbin/.klogd.
Sandbox analysis of payload from 203.0.113.88 returned clean verdict with low risk score.
